list.item: Find the absolute extrema of $$f$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,9} \right\rbrack$$ .
Find the absolute extrema of $$f$$ .

solution.paragraph: The function $$f$$ is continuous in its domain and differentiable on the interval $$\left( {0,9} \right)$$ . The derivative of $$f$$ is
$$f^{\prime}(x) = 1 - x^{- 1 \slash 2} = \frac{x^{1 \slash 2} - 1}{x^{1 \slash 2}}$$
and it is equal to zero when $$x = 1$$ . Evaluating $$f(x)$$ at the endpoints $$x = 0$$ and $$x = 9$$ and at the critical number $$1$$ of $$f$$ , we have
From these results, we see that $$- 1$$ is the absolute minimum value of $$f$$ and $$3$$ is the absolute maximum value of $$f$$ .

In this case, the domain of $$f$$ is the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,\infty} \right)$$ , which is not closed. Therefore, we resort to the graphical method. Using the techniques of graphing, we sketch the graph of $$f$$ in the accompanying figure.

problem.paragraph: Factory Operating Rate The operating rate (expressed as a percent) of factories, mines, and utilities in a certain region of the country on the $$t$$ th day of 2014 is given by the function
On which of the first $$250$$ days of 2014 was the operating rate highest?

solution.paragraph: The problem is solved by finding the absolute maximum of the function $$f$$ on $$\left\lbrack {0,250} \right\rbrack$$ . Differentiating $$f(t)$$ , we obtain

$$\begin{array}{l} {{f^{\prime}(t)} = \frac{\left( {t^{2} + 40,000} \right)(1200) - 1200t\left( {2t} \right)}{\left( t^{2} + 40,000 \right)^{2}}} \\ {\phantom{f^{\prime}(t)} = \frac{- 1200\left( {t^{2} - 40,000} \right)}{\left( t^{2} + 40,000 \right)^{2}}} \end{array}$$

Upon setting $$f^{\prime}(t) = 0$$ and solving the resulting equation, we obtain $$t = - 200$$ or $$200$$ . Since $$- 200$$ lies outside the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,250} \right\rbrack$$ , we are interested only in the critical number $$200$$ of $$f$$ . Evaluating $$f(t)$$ at $$t = 0$$ , $$t = 200$$ , and $$t = 250$$ , we find
We conclude that the operating rate was the highest on the $$200$$ th day of 2014—that is, a little past the middle of July 2014.
